preamble: Strengthening of the alveolar tap [ɾ] to a trill [r] in specific positions or speech styles. In Spanish, a coda rhotic, normally a tap, may be trilled in emphatic or oratorical speech (arma [ˈaɾma] ~ [ˈarma]). In Persian, the tap phoneme /ɾ/ has a trilled allophone [r] at the beginning of a word.

examples.note: Before consonants inside a word the tap is more frequent, but a trill occurs especially in emphatic or oratorical style, with no change in meaning.
The tap phoneme /ɾ/ has a trilled allophone at the start of a word, e.g. روز ruz 'day'; elsewhere the tap is usual.

sources: Wikipedia. Spanish phonology (Rhotics; citing Harris 1969, D'Introno et al. 1995, Canfield 1981). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_phonology
